title: 3D Airline Route Visualization (Flight Animation Along Arcs over a Globe)
prompt:
Use Three.js to display a network of cities and airline routes on a globe.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following import map in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Data]
(1) Hard-code exactly 20 cities: latitude and longitude + name + a continent field (such as Asia/Europe/Americas, etc.).
(2) Hard-code exactly 30 airline routes: each route connects two city indices or ids.

[Rendering]
(3) Use a sphere to represent Earth (textured or solid-colored).
(4) Represent cities as point Mesh objects on the sphere's surface.
(5) Represent airline routes as elevated arcs using QuadraticBezierCurve3 (or an equivalent approach) with TubeGeometry/Line, preventing them from passing through the sphere.
(6) Create looping flight animations along the routes (small airplanes/light points), with multiple activeFlights present simultaneously.

[Filtering]
(7) id="continentFilter": a select element or dropdown that filters the displayed airline routes and cities by continent ("all" means all continents).

[Interaction]
(8) Clicking an airline route or legend item must select a route and display its details in a details panel (id="routeDetail" may be used).

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  cityCount: number,
  routeCount: number,
  selectedRoute: null | number | string,
  activeFlights: number,
  filterContinent: string
}

cityCount=20 and routeCount=30; filterContinent must match the UI.

Output a single HTML file that can run when opened directly in a browser.
